stories.title: OCVibe Adds Five Dining Concepts to $5B SoCal District
stories.excerpt: The Samueli family has added five more dining concepts to the 50,000-square-foot market hall set to open next year as part of the $5 billion mixed-use development called OCVibe surrounding the Honda Center in Anaheim, Calif. Don Churros Gomez, MFK | Modern Filipino Kitchen, Mojo, Pull & Roll and Gelato Paradiso are the five new food options, adding Mexican, Filipino, Northern Chinese and Italian menus to the 21-kitchen market hall named Katella Commons. They join a growing roster at OCVibe, which earlier added concepts from chefs behind Amiga Amore, Burritos La Palma, Evil Cooks, Manaao Thai Comfort Food and Darkroom Restaurant and Wine Bar. Beloved Los Angeles chef Roy Choi is also bringing his Best Friend restaurant to the district. OCVibe did not disclose the values of the leases or the sizes of each space. OCVibe Senior Vice President Scott Frick recently told Commercial Observer that the Samueli family’s ownership structure has allowed the project to take a hands-on approach to restaurant leasing. Ownership is funding Katella Commons down to the kitchen equipment, allowing tenants to avoid substantial upfront costs of fitting out the new spaces. “Any tenant that comes in doesn’t have to come in with capital to fit out the kitchen — basically bring in your own knives and we’ll turn on the menu boards,” Frick said. That strategy is part of a broader effort to make OCVibe a year-round destination rather than a district that comes alive only when professional hockey team the Anaheim Ducks are playing. Frick said the project’s residential, office, hotel and entertainment components are intended to create a Monday-through-Sunday customer base for restaurants and other tenants. Katella Commons is expected to open in early 2027, following the debut of OCVibe’s concert hall, which can accommodate 5,000 people. bullets: Samueli family adding five dining concepts to 50K SF Katella Commons at $5B OCVibe, Anaheim
Mixed-use district surrounding Honda Center attracts chef Roy Choi's Best Friend and 21-kitchen market hall
Hands-on leasing approach by family ownership driving curated food-hall tenancy strategy
stories.summary: The Samueli family is expanding Katella Commons, a 50,000-square-foot market hall opening next year as part of the $5 billion OCVibe mixed-use development in Anaheim, with five new dining concepts (Don Churros Gomez, MFK Modern Filipino Kitchen, Mojo, Pull & Roll, Gelato Paradiso) joining previously announced chefs Roy Choi and others. The project's family ownership structure enables a hands-on approach to tenant curation and lease negotiation.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily supply, demand, or capital. This is primarily a hospitality/retail play; however, OCVibe's completion and placemaking success in Anaheim could support adjacent residential demand by strengthening the district's draw. Monitor whether residential rents in Anaheim sublets near Honda Center appreciate as the entertainment district matures.

stories.title: Massachusetts Biopharma Sees Capital Resurgence Even as Jobs Post First Annual Decline
stories.excerpt: Massachusetts’ biopharma industry saw employment shrink by 3.1% in 2025 to 113,503 jobs, the first annual decline in the two decades that industry association MassBio has tracked the sector. Conversely, MassBio’s 2026 Industry Snapshot found that venture capital, initial public offerings and M&A activity returned to the sector in force in the first half of 2026. Massachusetts-headquartered biopharma companies raised $3.45 billion in venture capital in H1 2026, up 25% year over year and the strongest opening half since 2023. The tally represented 25% of all U.S. biopharma VC, second only to California (43.4%). No other state reached 6%. Eight Massachusetts companies went public in the first half, matching the combined total of 2024 and 2025 and making up nearly two-thirds of all U.S. biotech IPOs. M&A value climbed sharply, with 11 Massachusetts companies acquired for a reported $18.0 billion, well above the $7.6 billion disclosed in the year-ago period. bullets: Massachusetts biopharma employment declined 3.1% in 2025 to 113,503 jobs, first annual drop in 20 years
VC funding surged 25% YoY to $3.45B in H1 2026; eight IPOs and $18B in M&A activity signal capital resurgence
Boston area holds 25% of U.S. biotech VC, second only to California, despite job contraction
stories.summary: Massachusetts biopharma sector posted its first annual employment decline in two decades in 2025 (down 3.1% to 113,503 jobs), but venture capital, IPOs, and M&A roared back in H1 2026: $3.45 billion in VC (+25% YoY), eight IPOs (matching 2024–2025 combined), and $18 billion in M&A acquisitions (vs. $7.6 billion year-ago). The sector accounted for 25% of all U.S. biotech VC.
stories.impact: Job contraction in Greater Boston's largest knowledge-sector employer threatens near-term residential demand growth and may pressure rents in life-sciences-dependent submarkets (Cambridge, Waltham, Watertown). However, strong capital reinflow and M&A consolidation suggest employers are restructuring rather than shrinking footprint; watch for selective hiring in biotech hubs and potential flight of junior talent out of market, which could weaken demand for Class A apartment supply targeting young professionals.

stories.title: Archer Aviation, AEG Partner on DTLA’s First Vertiport
stories.excerpt: AEG and Archer Aviation plan to develop Downtown Los Angeles’ first vertiport—a vertical takeoff and landing site for electric air taxis—at L.A. LIVE. The agreement, brokered by AEG Global Partnerships, makes Archer the exclusive air taxi partner of the four-million-square-foot sports and entertainment district. “Working with AEG on an iconic project like this vertiport at L.A. LIVE gives us the opportunity to continue building the infrastructure needed for Southern California to lead in the next era of all-electric flight,” said Archer’s founder and CEO, Adam Goldstein. AEG and Archer have completed the initial feasibility study for the L.A. LIVE site, including land-use and airspace reviews, power availability and community impact. The next phase, reviewing operational approach and guest experience, is currently underway as the partners work toward establishing the site as Los Angeles’ first downtown vertiport. Plans call for the vertiport to be ready in time for the LA28 Games. The post Archer Aviation, AEG Partner on DTLA’s First Vertiport appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: AEG and Archer Aviation planning Downtown LA's first vertiport at L.A. LIVE, four-million-SF mixed-use district
Initial feasibility study completed; operational design phase underway, target opening before LA28 Games 2028
Exclusive air-taxi partnership signals emerging urban mobility infrastructure attracting tech-forward development
stories.summary: AEG and Archer Aviation have partnered to develop Downtown Los Angeles' first vertiport—a vertical takeoff and landing facility for electric air taxis—at the L.A. LIVE entertainment district. The companies completed an initial feasibility study covering land use, airspace, power, and community impact; they are now refining operational and guest-experience design with plans to launch before the LA28 Games.
stories.impact: Minimal near-term impact on multifamily. However, successful vertiport operations at L.A. LIVE could enhance the district's prestige and draw, indirectly supporting demand for luxury residential in Downtown LA and nearby neighborhoods (Arts District, Little Tokyo) by positioning them as access points to emerging mobility infrastructure. This is a long-dated signal; monitor whether vertiport success drives corporate HQ or tech-talent migration to DTLA.

stories.title: NYC Unveils $4B Plan to Repair City-Owned Stretch of Brooklyn-Queens Expressway
stories.excerpt: Mayor Zohran Mamdani and New York City Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) Commissioner Mike Flynn announced plans to rehabilitate the 1.5-mile city-owned portion of the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway (BQE) between Atlantic Avenue and Sands Street. The $4-billion project, is epxected to take 10 years and to break ground in 2030. The infrastructure is 20 years past its design life and deteriorating under the weight of 130,000 vehicles every day, more than double the capacity for which it was designed, according to the mayor’s office. NYC DOT plans to build a temporary, two-level highway bypass on top of Furman Street, below the promenade, from Atlantic Avenue to Columbia Heights. “Time is up. We are fixing the triple cantilever,” Flynn said. At the New York Building Congress, president and CEO Carlo A. Scissura said, “The sooner we can get a shovel in the ground to deal with the disastrous BQE before it completely fails, the better and safer this city will be. And so the Building Congress applauds Mayor Mamdani, Deputy Mayor Kerson, Commissioner Flynn and the entire administration for bringing a plan to the table that aims at relieving the worst section of the city’s worst highway in the least time possible. While many questions remain about construction and timeline, they are 100% right to start the clock now on action.” The post NYC Unveils $4B Plan to Repair City-Owned Stretch of Brooklyn-Queens Expressway appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: NYC announcing $4B, 10-year BQE repair project, groundbreaking slated for 2030; infrastructure 20 years past design life
1.5-mile city-owned stretch between Atlantic Avenue and Sands Street deteriorating under 130K daily vehicles, double design capacity
Temporary two-level bypass on Furman Street planned to minimize disruption during reconstruction
stories.summary: New York City announced a $4 billion, decade-long rehabilitation of the 1.5-mile city-owned portion of the Brooklyn-Queens Expressway between Atlantic Avenue and Sands Street. The infrastructure is 20 years past its design life and carries 130,000 vehicles daily—more than double its intended capacity. Construction is expected to begin in 2030, with a temporary two-level bypass constructed on Furman Street.
stories.impact: Major supply-side headwind for multifamily developers in Brooklyn (DUMBO, Downtown Brooklyn, Park Slope, Sunset Park) and Queens (Long Island City, Astoria, Williamsburg corridor) during 2030–2040. A decade of highway construction will: (1) degrade pedestrian/transit access and livability along the BQE corridor, suppressing new multifamily feasibility and rent growth in adjacent submarkets; (2) reduce vehicle throughput, creating congestion that pushes commuter demand further away from the expressway, benefiting submarkets with superior transit alternatives (Crown Heights, Prospect Heights, Astoria, Ditmars); (3) delay residential project starts in high-opportunity blocks near the BQE until bypass operations are proven. Conversely, post-completion (2040+), expect significant repositioning demand and rent growth in previously underperformance corridors. Monitor early project cancellations or timelines shifted post-2030 in BQE-adjacent areas.

stories.title: The New School Sells Loeb Hall Residence to Hawkins Way Capital for $52M
stories.excerpt: In its third acquisition of student housing in Manhattan this summer, Hawkins Way Capital has purchased a residence hall near Union Square for $51.5 million from the New School, according to city records made public Tuesday. Hawkins, using the entity 135 E 12th Owner, bought Loeb Hall, a 268-bed residence hall at 131-135 East 12th Street, directly from The New School, records show. Joshua Bird, managing director and general counsel at Hawkins, signed the deal for the buyer, while Loretta Ferrari, chief financial officer at the New School, signed for the seller. “We’ve long been looking for the right opportunity in this neighborhood, and this property represents an ideal addition to our portfolio,” Ross Walker, managing partner at Hawkins, said in a statement to Commercial Observer. “Its location, existing student housing infrastructure and flexibility put us in an ideal position to deliver high-quality accommodations in one of the country’s strongest urban student housing markets.” It’s unclear why the New School stopped using Loeb Hall as an active dormitory for its students, but the property was removed from its undergraduate housing options this year. Loeb Hall is four blocks east of the New School’s main University Center and administrative offices on Fifth Avenue, although the sprawling urban campus has numerous sites near Union Square. The former Loeb Hall will undergo renovations and be repositioned under Hawkins’ Found Study student housing platform, according to a spokesperson for Hawkins. It’s unclear who brokered the recent sale. A spokesperson for the New School did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The deal is Hawkins’ third major student housing acquisition in Manhattan in recent months. bullets: Hawkins Way Capital acquires 268-bed Loeb Hall at 131-135 East 12th Street, Union Square, for $51.5M from The New School
Third Manhattan student housing acquisition by Hawkins this summer; property features existing residential infrastructure and neighborhood flexibility
Institutional investor consolidating student housing near NYU and Cooper Union zones
stories.summary: Hawkins Way Capital purchased Loeb Hall, a 268-bed student residence hall at 131-135 East 12th Street near Union Square, from The New School for $51.5 million. It is Hawkins' third Manhattan student housing acquisition this summer. The firm cited the property's location, existing infrastructure, and operational flexibility as key drivers.
stories.impact: Modest negative signal for core multifamily near Union Square and East Village. Hawkins' concentrated buying in student housing suggests institutional capital sees higher returns in purpose-built student dorms (long-dated, inflation-protected leases with universities) than in Class A apartments. This may compress cap rates on institutional student housing while reducing competition for near-campus multifamily assets. For multifamily developers, this signals: (1) student housing is an alternative hold strategy in college-adjacent markets; (2) younger professional rentals near universities face headwinds as institutional capital prioritizes locked-in student leases over open-market rentals; (3) The New School's asset sale may reflect balance-sheet pressures or portfolio rationalization, worth monitoring for other institutional divestitures in Manhattan student housing.

stories.title: Matterhorn Venture Partners Acquires Chicago Area Industrial Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Matterhorn Venture Partners announced a partnership with TPG AG U.S. Real Estate to acquire a portfolio of 16 Chicago-based industrial properties totaling approximately 986,000 square feet across the metropolitan area. The Chicago-based assets are part of a 53-building shallow bay industrial portfolio totaling approximately 5.4 million square feet, acquired for $628 million in partnership with TPG AG U.S. Real Estate, Redfearn Capital and Atlanta Property Group. The transaction is the largest to date for each of the three regional operating partners who will collaborate to manage the distribution, logistics and manufacturing facilities. MVP will asset manage the Chicago area assets, adding to the regional platform the firm has built with TPG AG since launching a programmatic joint venture earlier this year. “We see meaningful opportunity to grow income through mark-to-market on in-place rents, lease-up of existing vacancy, and targeted capital investment to improve tenant retention,” said Matt Kay, Co-Founder and Principal at Matterhorn Venture Partners. The post Matterhorn Venture Partners Acquires Chicago Area Industrial Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Matterhorn Venture Partners, TPG, Redfearn Capital, Atlanta Property Group acquire 53-building shallow-bay industrial portfolio, 5.4M SF, for $628M
Chicago area accounts for 16 buildings, 986K SF; Matterhorn will asset-manage regional platform
Strategy focused on mark-to-market rent growth, lease-up of existing vacancy, and targeted capital deployment
stories.summary: Matterhorn Venture Partners announced a partnership with TPG AG U.S. Real Estate, Redfearn Capital, and Atlanta Property Group to acquire a 53-building shallow-bay industrial portfolio totaling 5.4 million square feet for $628 million. The Chicago-area portion comprises 16 properties and approximately 986,000 square feet, which Matterhorn will manage. The sponsors aim to increase income through market-rent adjustments, vacancy lease-up, and targeted capital improvements.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily; however, this signals strong institutional appetite for industrial logistics real estate in Chicago. If industrial cap rates remain compressed and distribution-center rents accelerate due to e-commerce and supply-chain reshoring, construction costs and land prices in Chicago's industrial nodes (O'Hare, I-294 corridor, south suburbs) may rise, potentially crowding out multifamily development in lower-cost suburban pockets. Monitor whether rising industrial land values in Chicago's outer ring reduce greenfield multifamily feasibility in secondary submarkets.

stories.title: MetroStar Signs New Headquarters Lease at Reston Town Center
stories.excerpt: MetroStar Systems LLC, a Reston-based government IT contractor serving primarily defense and national security agencies, has signed a 37,844-square-foot lease at Reston Town Center.The new office, secured by JLL, will be located at 12010 Sunset Hills Road in Reston, Virginia, and represents the latest real estate move supporting MetroStar’s broader national growth plans and continued investment in expanding its capabilities and business following its acquisition by Veritas Capital in late 2025. JLL’s Jay Farmer and Steve Burman represented MetroStar in the transaction. BXP, the building owner, represented itself in the deal.MetroStar plans to relocate its Northern Virginia office to the new space in 2027 from its current location at 1856 Old Reston Avenue in Reston. The nine-story building is located in the heart of Reston Town Center, adjacent to the Reston Town Center Metro station, and features amenities including a fitness center. The post MetroStar Signs New Headquarters Lease at Reston Town Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: MetroStar Systems leases 37,844 SF at Reston Town Center, 12010 Sunset Hills Road, as new HQ following Veritas Capital acquisition (late 2025)
JLL brokered deal; expansion supports MetroStar's national growth in defense/national security IT services

stories.summary: MetroStar Systems, a Reston-based government IT contractor serving defense and national security agencies, signed a 37,844-square-foot headquarters lease at Reston Town Center (12010 Sunset Hills Road). The expansion follows MetroStar's late-2025 acquisition by Veritas Capital and is intended to support the firm's national growth and expanded capabilities.
stories.impact: Positive signal for Northern Virginia multifamily demand in the Northern Virginia submarket, particularly near Reston and the Route 7/Route 29 corridor. MetroStar's expansion under Veritas ownership suggests continued federal IT modernization spending and contractor growth in the region. Defense/national-security contractor hiring typically drives demand for Class A multifamily near office parks. However, the impact is modest because MetroStar's lease is only ~38K SF. Monitor broader federal IT contractor hiring and HQ moves to the Northern Virginia Tech Corridor (Dulles, Reston, Chantilly, Arlington) as leading indicators of sustained multifamily demand in the submarket.

stories.title: Fifth Third, CB&T TruAmerica Lend $124M on Bay Area Apartments Build
stories.excerpt: SummerHill Apartment Communities (SHAC) has landed $123.5 million of construction financing to build a multifamily project in the San Francisco Bay Area, Commercial Observer has learned. Fifth Third Bank and California Bank & Trust (CB&T) provided a $96.5 million senior construction loan for the developer’s planned apartment community in San Carlos, Calif. TruAmerica Multifamily also closed a $27 million preferred equity investment to support the six-story San Mateo County development, which is slated to commence construction soon. The deal marked TruAmerica Multifamily’s first preferred equity financing since launching a structured finance platform last year. The new business vertical was formed following the addition of Ash Baraghoush, head of TruAmerica’s structured finance group, after he spent nearly a decade at Pacific Urban Investors. “This really goes hand in hand with the firm’s transformation into being a residential investment management company and being able to speak throughout the entire capital stack as opposed to just being owner operators,” Baraghoush told Commercial Observer. “We have spent a good year-plus cultivating new relationships.” Located at 11 El Camino Real 24 miles south of Downtown San Francisco, the project will feature 251 apartments with 38 of the units designated as affordable housing. Baraghoush said San Carlos has plenty of tailwinds as a multifamily market given its close ties to the San Francisco Bay Area’s technology and life science industries. He noted that the San Carlos submarket has a 97 percent multifamily occupancy rate and the region has experienced double-digit rent growth. “The Bay Area as a market has certainly outperformed and is perhaps one of the one of the better performing markets in the nation right now driven by return to office and driven by the AI boom,” Baraghoush said. “The need for affordable workforce housing continues to remain and that’s one of the attractive natures for this
bullets: SummerHill Apartment Communities secures $123.5M construction financing: $96.5M senior loan (Fifth Third, CB&T) + $27M preferred equity (TruAmerica)
Six-story development in San Mateo County, California; TruAmerica's first preferred-equity deal under new structured-finance platform
Capital deployment signal: multifamily construction finance remains available in Bay Area despite higher rates and caps
stories.summary: SummerHill Apartment Communities has closed $123.5 million in construction financing for a six-story multifamily project in San Carlos, California. Fifth Third Bank and California Bank & Trust provided a $96.5 million senior construction loan, while TruAmerica Multifamily closed a $27 million preferred equity investment—the firm's first deal under its newly launched structured-finance platform. Construction is slated to commence soon.
stories.impact: Positive liquidity signal for Bay Area multifamily development. TruAmerica's entry into preferred-equity structuring and the syndication of construction debt across multiple lenders (Fifth Third, CB&T) indicate that intermediate capital is available for new apartment supply in the Bay Area, despite higher SOFR and cost of capital. However, the deal's size (~$123.5M) suggests moderate-scale developments remain fundable; mega-projects may face tighter terms. For developers: construction financing in Bay Area is available but likely at higher rates and with layered capital structures; monitor TruAmerica's continued preferred-equity appetite as a sign of broader structured-finance momentum in multifamily.

stories.title: Sports Tech Firm Genius Sports Moves U.S. HQ to Vornado’s 1290 Avenue of the Americas
stories.excerpt: Sports analytics and technology company Genius Sports is relocating its U.S. headquarters to 1290 Avenue of the Americas. The London-based company’s new 10-year lease with landlord Vornado Realty Trust spans 53,000 square feet across part of the tower’s sixth floor. Asking rent was $99 per square foot, according to The Real Deal, which first reported on the lease. Newmark’s Josh Berg and A.J. Dorn negotiated the deal on behalf of Genius Sports, while Vornado was represented in-house by Ryan Levy and Edward Riguardi. A spokesperson for the landlord declined to comment on the transaction. The deal offers Genius Sports a marked expansion from its 28,000-square-foot West Chelsea offices at 512 West 22nd Street. That building changed hands last year from Vornado and the Albanese Organization to Raghsa Real Estate for $205 million. Genius Sports’ arrival brings 1290 Avenue of the Americas to 95 percent occupancy. The 43-story, full-block building between 51st and 52nd streets is anchored by investment management firm Neuberger Berman, and recently underwent a $45 million renovation that updated lobby and building amenities. Vornado owns 70 percent of the building, while the Trump Organization holds a passive 30 percent stake. Other recent arrivals at the tower include business consulting firms Portage Point Partners and Protiviti, which CO reported leased a total of 93,000 square feet late last year. In January, investment manager Oaktree leased the building’s entire 12th floor, just a few stories below law firm Selendy Gay’s 101,000-square-foot offices. Spokespeople for Genius Sports and Newmark did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Genius Sports relocates U.S. HQ to Vornado's 1290 Avenue of the Americas, Manhattan; 53K SF, 10-year lease at $99/SF
Expansion from 28K SF West Chelsea (512 West 22nd Street, sold last year for $205M); brings 1290 to 95% occupancy
Sports-analytics tech company leasing demonstrates continued demand for premium office in Midtown Manhattan
stories.summary: London-based sports analytics and technology firm Genius Sports has leased 53,000 square feet at Vornado's 1290 Avenue of the Americas for its U.S. headquarters under a 10-year deal at $99 per square foot. The move represents a near-doubling from its prior 28,000-square-foot West Chelsea location. The lease brings the 43-story building to 95% occupancy.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily. However, Genius Sports' Midtown relocation signals sustained demand for premium office among tech and media firms, which typically employ younger professionals who rent apartments nearby (Hells Kitchen, Midtown West, Midtown East submarkets). Strong Midtown office leasing may support Class A rental demand in adjacent residential zones and suggest tech-talent in-migration to Manhattan, a positive for multifamily fundamentals. Monitor whether other tech and sports-media companies follow suit to Midtown; a broader tech-office uptick would support residential demand in transit-accessible neighborhoods near Midtown office concentrations.

stories.title: SJC Ventures Sells Whole Foods-Anchored Center in South Florida for $83M
stories.excerpt: SJC Ventures has sold a newly completed Whole Foods-anchored retail center in Doral, Fla., for $83 million, property records show. Called Doral Marketplace, the property spans 89,000 square feet at 10800 Northwest 41st Street, about a mile east of the Florida Turnpike and 14 miles west of Downtown Miami. Atlanta-based SJC Ventures completed the 10-acre strip mall last quarter. The sale excluded a 1.8-acre portion of the property leased to Chick-fil-A. Records list the buyer as Traditions Management, a Dallas-based developer and operator of senior living communities. The buyer assumed a loan with $50 million in outstanding debt, which has now been assigned to the Bank of Texas. Whole Foods is Doral Marketplace’s biggest tenant with a 43,000-square-foot location. Other tentants include J. Crew Factory, Ulta Beauty, Shake Shack, First Watch, GoodVets, The Spot Barbershop, Encore Nails, VIO MedSpa and Apizza Brooklyn Resto + Vino. The sale comes as Miami-Dade County retail leasing remains strong. During the second quarter of 2026, average asking rents jumped to $42.50 per square foot, up 2.6 percent quarter-over-quarter, while the vacancy rate fell to 3 percent. More than 1.3 million square feet of retail space remains under construction, including another Whole Foods location in South Beach, for which developer Russell Galbut nabbed a $54 million construction loan last year. Representatives for SJC Ventures and Traditions Management did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: SJC Ventures sells Doral Marketplace, Whole Foods-anchored 89K SF retail center, Doral, FL, to Traditions Management for $83M
Buyer (Dallas-based senior-living operator) assumed $50M debt; sale excludes 1.8-acre Chick-fil-A pad
Miami-Dade retail leasing strong; Q2 2026 asking rents jumped to $42.50/SF, up 2.6% QoQ
stories.summary: SJC Ventures sold Doral Marketplace, a newly completed 89,000-square-foot Whole Foods-anchored retail center in Doral, Florida, to Dallas-based Traditions Management (a senior-living developer/operator) for $83 million. The buyer assumed a $50 million loan now assigned to Bank of Texas. The sale excluded a 1.8-acre Chick-fil-A pad. Miami-Dade retail leasing remained strong in Q2 2026, with asking rents climbing to $42.50 per square foot.
stories.impact: Indirect negative signal for Miami-Dade multifamily development. A senior-living operator acquiring a retail asset suggests: (1) Traditions sees higher risk-adjusted returns in senior housing than in traditional multifamily, possibly reflecting compressed multifamily cap rates in Miami; (2) strong retail rents ($42.50/SF, up 2.6% QoQ) indicate land and construction costs may be rising in Doral, increasing development basis for new apartments and reducing feasibility margins. The Doral submarket (west of Turnpike, ~14 miles from Downtown) is secondary to core Miami multifamily zones (Brickell, Edgewater, Wynwood) but signals cost inflation across the metro. For developers: monitor whether strong retail fundamentals and buyer diversification (senior housing into retail) reflect scarcity of available land, which could push land prices higher and compress multifamily returns in Miami-Dade.
